In August this year Merlin, a flight control company developing commercial autonomous cargo operations, received a Part 146 Aircraft Design Organization certificate from the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand (CAANZ).

evidenceRecords.text: By Philip Butterworth-Hay es In September 2026 Joby Aviation announced its autonomous Cessna Caravan cargo aircraft had completed a USA 3,199-mile safari around the USA with zero control inputs from its onboard safety pilot, who sat and watched as the aircraft safely navigated its way around continental USA.

In August this year Merlin, a flight control company developing commercial autonomous cargo operations, received a Part 146 Aircraft Design Organization certificate from the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand (CAANZ).

This allows Merlin to internally approve aircraft design changes, streamlining the design approval process, putting the company on the fast track to launching commercial autonomous cargo operations with legacy aircraft.
If New Zealand wins the race to have autonomous cargo aircraft operating commercial service, it will be a huge feat.

In September 2026 Joby Aviation announced its autonomous Cessna Caravan cargo aircraft had completed a USA 3,199-mile safari around the USA with zero control inputs from its onboard safety pilot, who sat and watched as the aircraft safely navigated its way around continental USA.
This could happen as early as 2027.

In parallel and slightly behind the military, the FAA’s eVTOL Integration Pilot Program (eIPP) includes multiple uncrewed and crewed cargo operations, testing how these types can be safely integrated into the national airspace system, with a particular focus on the robustness and resilience of command and control (C2) and ATM links.

Once Merlin, Joby and Reliable Robotics (and others) have their autonomous flight control, C2 and ATM link systems certified for commercial operations, the pathway to large-aircraft cargo flights without pilots on board becomes clearer, though flight crew will still be needed – at least for the moment.

items.title: Japan Launches Seventh Taigei-Class Submarine as Nuclear Propulsion Debate Grows
items.originalTitle: Japan Launches Seventh Taigei-Class Submarine as Nuclear Propulsion Debate Grows
items.summary: On October 8, Japan’s Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) launched the seventh Taigei-class diesel-electric attack submarine, “Shogei” (しょうげい), for the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF), as Japan considers nuclear propulsion as a possible option for its future submarines. The Taigei-class employs the same torpedo countermeasures system incorporated into the last four Soryu-class submarines. It uses Japan’s newest Type 18 torpedo, which succeeds the Type 89. The new torpedo features improvements in propulsion, target detection, and processing.

evidenceRecords.text: On October 8, Japan’s Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) launched the seventh Taigei-class diesel-electric attack submarine, “Shogei” (しょうげい), for the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF), as Japan considers nuclear propulsion as a possible option for its future submarines.

The seventh Taigei-class submarine, “Shogei” (Credit: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries) Why Japan is considering nuclear-powered submarines The Taigei-class submarines use large-capacity lithium-ion batteries to improve their underwater endurance and operational capabilities.

In September 2025, a panel of experts advising the MoD recommended further research and technological development on VLS-equipped submarines, including consideration of what it described as “next-generation propulsion.” The recommendation did not explicitly call for nuclear propulsion, and Japan has not decided whether its future VLS-equipped submarines will be nuclear-powered.
The Taigei-class employs the same torpedo countermeasures system incorporated into the last four Soryu-class submarines.
It uses Japan’s newest Type 18 torpedo, which succeeds the Type 89.
The new torpedo features improvements in propulsion, target detection, and processing.
The class is also capable of launching the UGM-84L Harpoon Block II anti-ship missile against surface targets.
The missile has a reported range of 248 kilometers.
For now, Japan has made no decision to acquire nuclear-powered submarines.
The central question is what missions its future submarine force will be expected to perform, and which propulsion system would best meet those requirements while protecting the safety of its crews.

items.title: Nellis AFB renews UNIFY.C2 data fusion counter-UAS contract
items.originalTitle: Nellis AFB renews UNIFY.C2 data fusion counter-UAS contract
items.summary: Nellis Air Force Base has renewed its contract for UNIFY.C2, a counter-small UAS mission command platform developed by Spatial Persistent Software, following a year-long evaluation. The platform supports sensor fusion, track management, alerting and operational coordination across counter-uncrewed aircraft systems (C-UAS). The renewed contract will support C-UAS operations involving Nellis Air Force Base, Creech Air Force Base and the Nevada Test and Training Range.

items.originalTitle: British Commandos Emerge From German Submarine During Major NATO Exercise
items.summary: As part of the largest U.K. Commando Force exercise in 15 years, British special operators conducted a submarine insertion off Scotland, making use of a German Navy Type 212A — a boat you can read about in detail here . The submarine insertion, conducted at Cape Wrath on September 29, is part of Exercise Strike Warrior, a major NATO drill intended to rehearse allied crisis-response and warfighting operations across the North Atlantic and High North. British Commandos board the German U-boat off the north coast of Scotland during Strike Warrior 26.

items.title: Universal Quantum Raises Over $100 Million Series A
items.originalTitle: Universal Quantum Raises Over $100 Million Series A
items.summary: Insider Brief Universal Quantum raised more than $100 million in Series A funding to develop and commercialize its modular quantum computing technology and expand internationally. PRESS RELEASE — Universal Quantum , the company building large-scale quantum computing systems for real-world use, today announced it has secured over $100 million in Series A funding – marking the largest Series A ever raised by a quantum firm headquartered in the UK.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief Universal Quantum raised more than $100 million in Series A funding to develop and commercialize its modular quantum computing technology and expand internationally.

PRESS RELEASE — Universal Quantum , the company building large-scale quantum computing systems for real-world use, today announced it has secured over $100 million in Series A funding – marking the largest Series A ever raised by a quantum firm headquartered in the UK.
The funding will accelerate the company’s global expansion, as well as the development and commercialisation of its modular technology, advancing a path towards fault-tolerant quantum computing.

“ Universal Quantum ’s progress reflects our partners’ belief that we represent one of the most credible paths to quantum computing at scale,” said Dr Sebastian Weidt, CEO and co-founder of Universal Quantum.

“This round unites an extraordinary group of investors from the world’s most important pools of capital around a single mission: delivering utility-scale quantum computing.” The new capital will drive the continued development and commercialisation of Universal Quantum ’s modular approach to building the quantum computers needed for practical, error-corrected use – leveraging the company’s patented, world-record interconnect technology and advanced integrated chips to develop the chiplet arrays and control systems required to reduce engineering risk and accelerate the path to larger-scale

The funding will also support Universal Quantum ’s recently announced expansion in Singapore , where it is establishing its first R&D centre outside Europe, as well as expansion in the United States, Japan and across its German hub in Hamburg.
Solving the problem of scale Universal Quantum was founded on the belief that scale is the major challenge in quantum computing.

Universal Quantum ’s approach is designed to connect these modules in a practical, manufacturable way, creating a route to the scale needed for fault-tolerant quantum computing and giving industry partners a clearer path to quantum utility.

A global investment story Universal Quantum was founded in 2018 by Professor Sebastian Weidt and Professor Winfried Hensinger of the University of Sussex, co-authors of the first practical blueprint for a large-scale trapped-ion quantum computer, published in 2017.

Universal Quantum ’s Series A brings together one of the most geographically and strategically diverse investor syndicates assembled in the quantum sector, including: DCVC – the leading Silicon Valley venture firm that defined the term “Deep Tech”, backing breakthrough hard-science companies across two decades, including most nationally critical quantum technology companies in the US; Firgun Ventures – a quantum-focused investor with significant sovereign backing and strong academic partners; EDBI – the Singapore-based sovereign investor, underscoring Asia’s strategic commitment to frontier

“ Universal Quantum brings together world-class scientific leadership with an exceptionally clear approach to quantum computing,” said Zeynep Korutürk, Founding & Managing Partner of Firgun Ventures .

With Europe under pressure to prove it can compete on frontier technologies, we are proud to invest in a European company that has grown into a global player, one that is well positioned to help define the future of industrial-scale quantum computing.” Universal Quantum ’s raise reflects a broader shift that has seen the flow of serious institutional capital into quantum computing.

items.title: Hindustan Shipyard Launches First Fleet Support Ship ‘Surya’ for Indian Navy
items.originalTitle: Hindustan Shipyard Launches First Fleet Support Ship ‘Surya’ for Indian Navy
items.summary: India’s Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL) launched the Indian Navy’s first Fleet Support Ship (FSS-1), Surya, on October 6, 2026, at a ceremony attended by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh as the chief guest. HSL also laid the keel of the fifth Fleet Support Ship (FSS-5) on October 6, 2026. The company also inaugurated several upgraded facilities, including an upgraded slipway and a 300-tonne Goliath crane, as part of efforts by India’s Ministry of Defence (MoD) to enhance the performance of the state-owned shipyard in Visakhapatnam, the country’s naval hub.

evidenceRecords.text: India’s Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL) launched the Indian Navy’s first Fleet Support Ship (FSS-1), Surya , on October 6, 2026, at a ceremony attended by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh as the chief guest.
Representative image of a Fleet Support Ship for the Indian Navy by design consultant firm SEDS.
The Fleet Support Ships are intended to provide at-sea replenishment and sustained logistical support to naval operations.

India’s Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL) launched the Indian Navy’s first Fleet Support Ship (FSS-1), Surya, on October 6, 2026, at a ceremony attended by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh as the chief guest.
HSL also laid the keel of the fifth Fleet Support Ship (FSS-5) on October 6, 2026.

The company also inaugurated several upgraded facilities, including an upgraded slipway and a 300-tonne Goliath crane, as part of efforts by India’s Ministry of Defence (MoD) to enhance the performance of the state-owned shipyard in Visakhapatnam, the country’s naval hub.
The upgraded slipway will enable HSL to build and launch ships of up to 45,000 DWT.
Meanwhile, the Kone Goliath crane, designed and manufactured by L&T Geostructure, will be used for the precise handling of heavier blocks during modern block construction.
L&T’s shipbuilding arm is also a major subcontractor for the FSS program, building components for two ships under a contract with HSL.

Getting such clocks to work, however, proved no easy feat, because driving these narrow nuclear transitions requires highly stable lasers with extremely small bandwidths. Getting such clocks to work, however, proved no easy feat, because driving these narrow nuclear transitions requires highly stable lasers with extremely small bandwidths.

They thus created stabilized nuclear clocks that they could compare continuously to frequency standards derived from atomic clocks.
Their results set limits on how dark matter can couple to photons and the strong nuclear force that are comparable to those derived from today’s best atomic clocks.

He is also interested in creating a trapped-ion thorium nuclear clock that would be more isolated from its environment and could re-use many of the quantum control techniques developed for atomic and ion clocks.
Victor Flambaum , a theorist from the University of New South Wales, Australia who was not involved in either project, calls the teams’ devices the “first prototypes of nuclear clocks”.

displayTranslation.sourceTitle: Federal Ammunition, Mossberg and Palladyne AI develop autonomous airborne C-UAS
displayTranslation.sourceSummary: Federal Ammunition, Mossberg and Palladyne AI have announced the joint development of SwarmShot, a modular autonomous airborne counter-UAS system designed to turn compatible drones into reusable air-to-air interceptors. The system will combine Federal’s counter-uncrewed aircraft system (C-UAS) ammunition, a lightweight Mossberg weapon module and Palladyne AI’s IntelliSwarm autonomy system. It will initially be developed as a mission module for Palladyne AI’s Gremlin-X Group 1 quadcopter, with the companies planning an integration kit for compatible third-party aircraft following qualification.

items.title: A2Z Drone Delivery selected for Grab Indonesia’s BVLOS food delivery trial
items.originalTitle: A2Z Drone Delivery selected for Grab Indonesia’s BVLOS food delivery trial
items.summary: A2Z Drone Delivery has commenced a beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) food delivery pilot being operated by Grab Indonesia and drone services provider SKYY Network in Bali. The trial connects Café del Mar Bali with Nuanu Creative City, with customers placing orders through Grab’s app. SKYY Network is operating the flights under a certificate issued by Indonesia’s Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA). The partners describe the project as Indonesia’s first BVLOS food delivery operation.

The Longtail Dual features a dual-battery architecture designed to provide redundancy, while the AirDocks autonomously launch, recover and recharge the aircraft between missions.

items.summary: Insider Brief Zumo and Quantum Chain have partnered to explore quantum-secure financial infrastructure and digital asset applications in the UK. The collaboration will examine integrating Quantum Chain ’s quantum-secure blockchain infrastructure with Zumo’s digital asset infrastructure for regulated financial institutions. PRESS RELEASE — Zumo and Quantum Chain have teamed up to explore opportunities for quantum-secure financial infrastructure in the United Kingdom.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief Zumo and Quantum Chain have partnered to explore quantum-secure financial infrastructure and digital asset applications in the UK.
The collaboration will examine integrating Quantum Chain ’s quantum-secure blockchain infrastructure with Zumo’s digital asset infrastructure for regulated financial institutions.
PRESS RELEASE — Zumo and Quantum Chain have teamed up to explore opportunities for quantum-secure financial infrastructure in the United Kingdom.

The collaboration brings together Quantum Chain ’s quantum-secure blockchain infrastructure with Zumo’s digital asset infrastructure and experience supporting enterprise and institutional applications spanning quantum-secure private networks, digital currencies and tokenized assets.

As financial institutions continue to adopt blockchain-based infrastructure for payments, deposits and digital assets, the collaboration will focus on ensuring Zumo’s services remain secure and resilient against emerging threats, including those posed by quantum computing.

The collaboration will explore: Quantum-secure digital assets: Integrate Zumo and Quantum Chain to support quantum safe digital asset management across central banks, banks and regulated institutions.

Nick Jones, Founder and CEO of Zumo, said: “The UK is preparing for the full implementation of its regulatory regime for cryptoassets, which will unlock the growing institutional appetite we’re seeing for digital assets.” Zumo provides the compliant infrastructure that helps financial institutions to responsibly launch new propositions.

By partnering with Quantum Chain we can ensure they are protected against both quantum threats and sophisticated AI-led cyberattacks, which are converging.” Max Denega, Founder and CEO of Quantum Chain , confirms: “As a British citizen and military veteran, bringing quantum-secure infrastructure for UK finance home is a step towards a stronger British ecosystem.
Quantum Chain sits at the convergence of post-quantum security, blockchain and finance with infrastructure designed for a future-proof on-chain global financial system.

items.title: Embraer, Lockheed Martin vie for India’s $10.5B military transport aircraft deal
items.originalTitle: Embraer, Lockheed Martin vie for India’s $10.5B military transport aircraft deal
items.summary: NEW DELHI — Global aerospace companies Embraer from Brazil and Lockheed Martin from the United States are offering to expand aircraft manufacturing facilities in India as they pursue an approximately $10.5 billion contract for 60 medium transport aircraft for the Indian Air Force. Embraer’s C-390 Millennium is competing with Lockheed Martin’s C-130J Super Hercules as India seeks to replace its aging military transport fleet that includes the Soviet-era Antonov An-32. Lockheed Martin already has a presence in India — the Indian Air Force currently operates 12 C-130J Super Hercules aircraft.

evidenceRecords.text: NEW DELHI — Global aerospace companies Embraer from Brazil and Lockheed Martin from the United States are offering to expand aircraft manufacturing facilities in India as they pursue an approximately $10.5 billion contract for 60 medium transport aircraft for the Indian Air Force.
Embraer’s C-390 Millennium is competing with Lockheed Martin’s C-130J Super Hercules as India seeks to replace its aging military transport fleet that includes the Soviet-era Antonov An-32.
Lockheed Martin already has a presence in India — the Indian Air Force currently operates 12 C-130J Super Hercules aircraft.
Besides ferrying troops, vehicles and ammunition, India also uses military transport aircraft for disaster relief and humanitarian assistance.
The company says the aircraft it is now offering, the C-130J-30 in its Block 8.1.2 configuration, will be more advanced than the ones currently with the air force.
India has set a requirement of minimum 40% domestic content for the aircraft.
Because the country shares long Himalayan borders with rivals Pakistan and China, the aircraft must also be able to operate in high-altitude locations and from temporary or unpaved strips.

PRESS RELEASE — IBM (NYSE: IBM ) today announced it has been selected for Stage C, the third phase of the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) led by DARPA, the United States Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency.

This phase will advance IBM through DARPA’s verification process, in which independent experts extensively test and measure quantum hardware, technology, systems engineering, and architectures to determine if a company can build a fault-tolerant quantum computer.

“Advancing to the third stage of DARPA’s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative validates the strength of IBM ‘s path to building a fault-tolerant quantum computer,” said Jay Gambetta, Director of IBM Research and IBM Fellow.
For more information about the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, visit the DARPA website .

PRESS RELEASE — IBM (NYSE: IBM) today announced it has been selected for Stage C, the third phase of the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) led by DARPA, the United States Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency.

“Advancing to the third stage of DARPA’s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative validates the strength of IBM‘s path to building a fault-tolerant quantum computer,” said Jay Gambetta, Director of IBM Research and IBM Fellow.

As an independent research and development arm of the U.S. Department of Defense, DARPA launched the QBI in 2024 to determine whether an industrially useful faulttolerant quantum computer can be built by 2033.
The program defines such a system as one whose computational value will exceed its cost.
IBM has successfully progressed through the QBI’s assessment process, including the first two stages that analyzed comprehensive R&D plans and risk mitigation approaches.
Last year, IBM laid out its plans to deliver the world’s first fault-tolerant quantum computer, IBM Quantum Starling.
Starling will combine advances in error correction, processor design, systems engineering, and more.
Since then, IBM’s progression has remained on course, including the demonstration of core hardware components for fault tolerance and breakthroughs in efficient error correction decoding.
For more information about the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, visit the DARPA website.

items.summary: During his time as the lead propulsion engineer for SR-71 Blackbirds at NASA’s Dryden Flight Research Center , Tim Conners looked into how to push the iconic recon plane to fly faster than it had ever flown before. It was set by a Blackbird in 1976 “on a straight-line course over Edwards Air Force Base in California .” In a recent interview with TWZ , Conners said he investigated whether there were ways to get Blackbird to approach Mach 4, equivalent to roughly a whopping 2,660 mph at altitude.

evidenceRecords.text: During his time as the lead propulsion engineer for SR-71 Blackbirds at NASA’s Dryden Flight Research Center , Tim Conners looked into how to push the iconic recon plane to fly faster than it had ever flown before.

It was set by a Blackbird in 1976 “on a straight-line course over Edwards Air Force Base in California .” In a recent interview with TWZ , Conners said he investigated whether there were ways to get Blackbird to approach Mach 4, equivalent to roughly a whopping 2,660 mph at altitude.

Fast forward to today, with the possibility that NASA could be returning the SR-71 in some configuration to its test fleet, as well as its potential missions, the question of just how fast could the airframe go has become far more relevant than just a hypothetical exercise.

Conners spoke to us about his knowledge of plans to restore SR-71 #844, which had mysteriously disappeared from NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center, as well as its potential uses, in a deep-dive interview here .

Prior to the revelations about the missing Blackbird, speculation about NASA’s renewed interest in the type was sparked last month, when NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman showed the silhouette of an aircraft that immediately drew comparisons to SR-71 during a speech at the annual All-In Summit in Los Angeles, California.

Isaacman pushed back on a direct link to the SR-71 but said his agency is working hard to get “back in the business of flying high and fast again.” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman talks at the All-In Summit about new high- and fast-flying X-planes with the eye-catching aircraft silhouette in the background.
All-In Summit/YouTube screencap Given that, we wanted to know what limited the SR-71’s speed in its original configuration and how fast Conners thought it could go with modifications.

If you look at the flight envelope, that defines the right edge of the envelope.” SR-71 Blackbird. (Courtesy photo via USAF) “The engines, however, were optimized to fly at about 500 knots equivalent airspeed, 475 to 500, and for whatever reason, there was a mismatch between what the engines were designed to do and what the airframe was ultimately optimized for, which was flight at around 450 knots,” the engineer added.

That limitation was driven primarily by the material strength of the engine front frame, from what it was described to me, and that’s what drove the analysis we did at NASA.” SR-71 tail number 844 during its service with NASA. (NASA) To even consider pushing the aircraft past the world record speed, Conners said something had to be done to mitigate the tremendous effects of the extreme heat on the air entering the engines.

If we’re looking at alternate engines designed to handle the higher Mach capability, then that could put the limiter on the airframe at that point, which we were told at NASA was somewhere like up near Mach 4 for brief excursions.” Aviation expert Paul F.
Temperature was just one factor in limiting how fast the SR-71 could travel, Crickmore explained.

items.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
items.originalTitle: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
items.summary: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms. Back in 2022, ESA reported that Solar Orbiter had spotted a kink in the solar wind’s magnetic field known as a ‘switchback’. While switchbacks have been spotted often near the Sun, scientists are still debating how they form.

evidenceRecords.text: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field.

By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
Back in 2022, ESA reported that Solar Orbiter had spotted a kink in the solar wind’s magnetic field known as a ‘switchback’.
While switchbacks have been spotted often near the Sun, scientists are still debating how they form.
By watching from afar, Solar Orbiter helped solve a piece of this puzzle, confirming the switchback to be S-shaped: something scientists had predicted but not seen directly.

The spacecraft has now added another crucial piece to this puzzle by tracing a switchback back to its source at the Sun. “Solar Orbiter flew through a very large switchback,” says Jesse Coburn of CNRS/LPP, France, lead author of the new paper. “Because of this, we were able to sample rarely observed particles there that have tell-tale fingerprints of their origin.”

To make the discovery, the researchers studied in situ observations of the switchback’s particles from Solar Orbiter’s SWA, analysed images of the Sun’s disc, and modelled the magnetic fields of both the Sun and surrounding space.

They created a new model to identify where the plasma came from; this model connected the measurements from Solar Orbiter to data from NASA’s Solar Dynamics Observatory to reveal the switchback’s solar source in unprecedented detail.
‘On the Coronal Origin of Magnetic Switchbacks in the Solar Wind’ by Jesse T.
Coburn et al. is published today in Nature Astronomy.

items.originalTitle: Haiqu Releases AgenticOS to Plan and Check Quantum Research
items.summary: Insider Brief Haiqu launched AgenticOS, a system that coordinates specialized AI agents to plan, validate and prepare quantum research experiments for hardware execution under human oversight. In a chemistry test, Haiqu reported that four of 10 unassisted AI agent runs violated setup instructions, while AgenticOS maintained the approved protocol and produced a simulated result within approximately 3.4% of an exact reference.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief Haiqu launched AgenticOS, a system that coordinates specialized AI agents to plan, validate and prepare quantum research experiments for hardware execution under human oversight.

In a chemistry test, Haiqu reported that four of 10 unassisted AI agent runs violated setup instructions, while AgenticOS maintained the approved protocol and produced a simulated result within approximately 3.4% of an exact reference.

Haiqu reported that AgenticOS developed and ran a 3-by-3 Hubbard model experiment on an IBM quantum computer, reducing circuit depth by 75% and proposing a calibration that aligned hardware results with an error-free simulation of the same method.
Today, Haiqu is addressing that by unveiling AgenticOS , giving quantum researchers a team of AI agents that are built for scientific exploration, and designed to catch mistakes before they happen.

With the Haiqu AgenticOS, researchers can now design an entire quantum project — from the initial question to an experiment that’s ready for quantum hardware — and assign multiple teams of AI agents to validate and confirm the research findings every step of the way.

“AgenticOS takes on much of that labor-intensive work, freeing up researchers so they can spend their time working on the right questions, reaching results much faster without sacrificing accuracy.” AgenticOS builds on the Haiqu platform announced in May .

A researcher starts with a question, and the system assigns teams of specialized AI agents to review the literature, work through first-principles mathematical derivations, assess quantum feasibility and check the results.
Haiqu’s AgenticOS shows its investigative process as a map of connected research tasks.

During a recent chemistry study accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop in Paris focused on AI for Scientific Discovery, Haiqu demonstrated the need for its platform by giving leading AI agents the same research brief, with and without AgenticOS.
Using Haiqu’s AgenticOS, the same models held to the approved protocol from start to finish and produced a simulated quantum result within approximately 3.4% of the exact diagonalization reference.
“Being able to organize, ground and check an AI agent’s work matters as much for scientific research as improving the models themselves,” said Richard Givhan, co-founder and CEO of Haiqu.
Starting from a scientist’s idea, AgenticOS built the experiment on a 3-by-3 grid, small enough to cross-check against an exact classical solution, and ran it on an IBM quantum computer.

evidenceRecords.text: Source: PTC Global energy company Schneider Electric this week said it will acquire industrial design, engineering, and data management firm PTC Inc. for about $22.6 billion.

The Boston-based companies claimed that the combination will bridge the “digital and physical worlds across the lifecycle, from design and build to operate and maintain.” Schneider Electric said it will be better able to serve industry with digitalization and AI , combining its operational expertise with PTC’s design and data intelligence.

Acquisitions could help Schneider compete with Siemens The PTC deal could help Schneider Electric compete with Siemens and other global leaders in industrial automation and software in sectors such as aerospace and defense , noted Matthieu Kulezak, a senior analyst at Interact Analysis .

“Together with AVEVA and the proposed Cognite acquisition, it could connect engineering decisions with how products are manufactured, operated and maintained.” PTC Onshape gives Schneider access to robotics developers and machine-building teams, while PTC ‘s Codebeamer supports requirements, testing, and traceability for increasingly complex software-driven products, Kulezak added.

“AVEVA’s experience within the group should help, but Schneider will also need to manage adjacent capabilities across AVEVA and Cognite without slowing innovation.” PTC gives Schneider Electric a shortcut from industrial operations into product engineering, strengthening its challenge to Siemens and Dassault Systèmes.

items.originalTitle: German Bundeswehr: A new naval port in Emden
items.summary: After months of evaluating different locations, the German Minister of Defense Boris Pistorius has now announced that the Bundeswehr's new naval port will be built in Emden on the North Sea coast of Lower Saxony. He noted that a new port is needed to accommodate the growing German Navy: new ships and boats require berths, and additional service members need housing. The commercial port of Emden is the economic heart of East Frisia. Emden hosted a Bundeswehr base until 1997, but it was no longer needed after the end of the Cold War and was consequently decommissioned.

evidenceRecords.text: Citing the escalating security threat, the German Navy has decided to establish a second port on the North Sea coast.

After months of evaluating different locations, the German Minister of Defense Boris Pistorius has now announced that the Bundeswehr's new naval port will be built in Emden on the North Sea coast of Lower Saxony.
He noted that a new port is needed to accommodate the growing German Navy: new ships and boats require berths, and additional service members need housing.
The commercial port of Emden is the economic heart of East Frisia.
Emden hosted a Bundeswehr base until 1997, but it was no longer needed after the end of the Cold War and was consequently decommissioned.
"Emden offers the opportunity to build a dedicated naval port that complies with the latest requirements, including those for security and port protection," Peters emphasizes in an interview with DW.
The only naval port currently on the German North Sea coast is located in Wilhelmshaven.

From a strategic perspective, it doesn't make sense to have just one port and nothing to fall back on, security expert Peters emphasized. "If some kind of scenario where conflict breaks out were to actually occur and this infrastructure were to fail, then you'd have a real problem.
That's why they want to diversify their options here now."

Defense Minister Boris Pistorius also emphasized the strategic advantage of a second naval port on the North Sea: "This makes us harder to predict in an emergency and expands our operational capabilities."
The planned port in Emden is intended to complement and provide relief for the Wilhelmshaven naval base.
This is where Operational Flotilla 2 is stationed, a large formation consisting of frigates and supply ships.
The Wilhelmshaven naval base is also being expanded as the fleet grows and personnel levels increase.
Although it will not be getting a naval base, the German government is investing a great deal of money there as well.
Construction of the naval port is likely to take years.

Mayor Tim Kruithoff was all the more delighted: "This is a great day for Emden." He described the planned naval base as "an extraordinary opportunity" for jobs and for the economic development of the entire region.

The UK’s military is too focused on global commitments at the expense of domestic defence, meaning the government’s planned increase in defence spending is likely to result in even greater waste, a thinktank report has warned.

Calling this a symptom of a “destructive, outdated foreign policy” centred on overseas missions which have often made the globe less safe, the report says the imminent uptick in spending should be accompanied by a change of stance, with a much bigger focus on domestic defence.
It questions whether more of the new money should be used for domestic defence, and whether the focus on overseas missions has even made the UK safer.
“Britain should end its support for these attempts at global policing.
Instead, it should focus its military resources on defence and its public investment on health, housing and the climate emergency.”
There is an awareness of the importance of avoiding waste among defence officials, including the risk that an arbitrary focus on reaching a certain level of spending could exacerbate this.

Since computer use burns through large amounts of tokens, a cheap, fast model like Haiku 5.5 is a natural fit.
Anthropic also lists OpenAI's budget model GPT-6 Luna as a comparison, and Haiku 5.5 leads across every tested category.
Sonnet 5.5 reference scores show, however, that Haiku 5.5 still falls well behind Anthropic's larger model.

items.originalTitle: Eclipse Qrisp Wins Quantum Effects Award 2026 for Quantum Software
items.summary: Insider Brief Eclipse Foundation, an open-source quantum programming framework initiated by Fraunhofer FOKUS, won the 2026 Quantum Effects Award in the Quantum Computing Software & Algorithms category. PRESS RELEASE — The Eclipse Foundation , one of the world’s largest open source software foundations, today announced that Eclipse Qrisp , an open source framework for high-level quantum programming initiated by Fraunhofer FOKUS , has won the Quantum Effects Award 2026 in the Quantum Computing Software & Algorithms category. Eclipse Qrisp moves quantum programming up the software stack.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief Eclipse Foundation, an open-source quantum programming framework initiated by Fraunhofer FOKUS, won the 2026 Quantum Effects Award in the Quantum Computing Software & Algorithms category.

PRESS RELEASE — The Eclipse Foundation , one of the world’s largest open source software foundations, today announced that Eclipse Qrisp , an open source framework for high-level quantum programming initiated by Fraunhofer FOKUS , has won the Quantum Effects Award 2026 in the Quantum Computing Software & Algorithms category.
Eclipse Qrisp moves quantum programming up the software stack.
This award is tremendous recognition for Fraunhofer FOKUS and the Eclipse Qrisp community.” The Quantum Effects Award recognises application-oriented innovation in quantum technologies.

Moving Quantum Programming up the Software Stack Qrisp abstracts much of the complexity of working directly with individual qubits and gates through higher-level constructs such as typed quantum variables, functions, automatic memory management, and control flow.
Building an Open Quantum Software Ecosystem As quantum hardware and software evolve rapidly, Qrisp provides an open, vendor-neutral platform for building quantum algorithms.

Eclipse Qrisp is also contributing to SecQDevOps , a Horizon Europe project exploring how security, testing, compliance, and DevOps practices can be integrated across quantum software and hardware development.

Qrisp provides a high-level programming layer that can target different quantum computing backends, supporting this broader effort to make quantum software development more systematic, secure, and scalable.

items.originalTitle: Google says 180 billion images and videos now carry SynthID watermarks as detector goes public
items.summary: Anyone can now check whether an image, video, or audio file was created by Google's AI or its partners. Google has opened its SynthID Detector to the public. The tool spots invisible watermarks embedded in content from models like Gemini, Veo, or Lyria and supports JPG, PNG, MP4, and MP3. SynthID isn't a universal AI detector. OpenAI, Nvidia, and Kakao also use SynthID for media. For text detection, OpenAI developed its own system.

items.originalTitle: NASA Selects GIMLI to Search the Marius Lunar Pit for a Potential Lunar Base Site
items.summary: The chief aim of NASA's Artemis Program is to create a "sustained program of lunar exploration and development." Beyond returning astronauts to the Moon for the first time since the Apollo Era, NASA and other space agencies hope to build the infrastructure that will enable regular, long-duration missions to the lunar surface. evidenceRecords.text: The chief aim of NASA's Artemis Program is to create a "sustained program of lunar exploration and development." Beyond returning astronauts to the Moon for the first time since the Apollo Era, NASA and other space agencies hope to build the infrastructure that will enable regular, long-duration missions to the lunar surface.
In addition to targeting the South Pole-Aitken Basin, NASA is eyeing lunar caves as a potential site for habitats and other lunar facilities.
Meanwhile, space agencies need to send large amounts of cargo and robotic explorers to the surface.

This includes the Geophysical Instruments for Marius Lunar pit Investigation (GIMLI), a Planetary Science Institute-led proposal that will investigate a "skylight," a hole in an old lunar lava tube, to see if a large cave system extends beyond it.
Such a location could provide a safe place for astronauts to operate on the surface in the future.
Observations from lunar orbit have provided compelling evidence that caves and lava tubes may exist under the Moon’s surface.
GIMLI’s research will focus on the Marius Hill Pit (MHP), a large hole in one of the Moon’s most volcanically diverse regions.
Like other lunar pits, MHP may serve as an opening to these underground spaces, which may have formed during ancient volcanic activity.
One in particular is the Marius Hill Pit (MPH), a prominent skylight on the nearside's Oceanus Procellarum.
GIMLI will allow scientists to investigate MHP directly from the lunar surface using an advanced suite of instruments.
These include ground-penetrating radar, seismic sensors, a gravimeter to probe beneath the surface, and cameras that provide imagery of the surface and pit walls.
These will allow the mission team not only to search for an underground recess, but also to determine its size (should one exist).

items.summary: Researchers in the Netherlands have shown that they can turn off the dipole moment of molecules that are normally polar, drastically altering the molecules’ behaviour in low-energy collisions. In 2023 experimental physicist Bas van de Meerakker and theorist colleagues at the Radboud University Nijmegen in the Netherlands shone a ray of light on this murky area by studying the collision cross-section (that is, the likelihood that collisions will take place) between molecules of ammonia (NH 3 ) at low energies.

In 2023 experimental physicist Bas van de Meerakker and theorist colleagues at the Radboud University Nijmegen in the Netherlands shone a ray of light on this murky area by studying the collision cross-section (that is, the likelihood that collisions will take place) between molecules of ammonia (NH 3 ) at low energies.

A big turn off The Radboud team explained this discrepancy by noting that in the classical picture, polar molecules such as ammonia have a permanently asymmetric charge distribution – a dipole moment – due to the arrangement of the bonds between their constituent atoms.

According to this quantum picture, collisions between polar molecules at high speeds (high energies) cause these opposite parity states to mix via interactions between the molecules’ electrostatic fields.
In his view, the results support the idea that effective dipolar interactions become strongly suppressed at low collision energies.

By incorporating a statistical method for correcting incomplete satellite data, the researchers developed an approach that can estimate structural damage immediately after a disaster without requiring a separate, computationally expensive training stage.
In actual disaster settings, however, complete satellite imagery is not always available.
Portions of satellite images may be obscured by clouds, smoke, precipitation, shadows and other factors, which can reduce the performance of subsequent AI or statistical analyses.

Existing AI-based damage assessment methods also often require large volumes of training data and substantial computational resources, making them difficult to deploy for immediate damage prediction in the aftermath of a disaster.

To address these challenges, the research team combined a Scientific AI approach, which integrates structural engineering knowledge into artificial intelligence, with a general-purpose statistical imputation method that rapidly corrects incomplete data.
Rather than simply learning from data, Scientific AI incorporates engineering knowledge of the physical phenomenon of structural damage into AI-based analysis.

In particular, it uses image entropy, a measure of disorder in satellite imagery, to analyze the extent of changes in structures and their surrounding environments before and after a disaster and to predict structural damage at the city scale.
The researchers also applied a statistical data imputation method to enable damage prediction even when parts of satellite imagery are obscured or missing.
This makes it possible to predict disaster damage even from satellite imagery in which some information has been lost because of clouds, smoke or other obstructions.

A key feature of the framework is that, unlike state-of-the-art AI approaches, it does not require a costly training stage in which large-scale data sets must be newly assembled and used to train a model.

Instead of building extensive training data sets and retraining a model whenever a new disaster occurs, the framework can immediately estimate damage using pre- and post-disaster satellite imagery and publicly available data.

The significance of this work lies in treating disaster damage prediction not simply as a problem of interpreting satellite imagery or training artificial intelligence models, but as a Scientific AI problem that integrates structural engineering knowledge with statistical data correction techniques.

items.title: Spiking neural network learns to predict what will happen, when, and how likely it is
items.originalTitle: Spiking neural network learns to predict what will happen, when, and how likely it is
items.summary: Imagine hearing a familiar sound and expecting something to happen. Before the event arrives, the brain can predict what it will be, when it will occur and how likely it is. Yet computational models often treat these questions separately or use learning methods that are difficult to reconcile with biological circuits. A new study proposes an alternative in which one population of spiking neurons learns all three together. The model successfully combined the three dimensions of prediction.

evidenceRecords.text: Imagine hearing a familiar sound and expecting something to happen.
Before the event arrives, the brain can predict what it will be, when it will occur and how likely it is.
Yet computational models often treat these questions separately or use learning methods that are difficult to reconcile with biological circuits.
A new study proposes an alternative in which one population of spiking neurons learns all three together.
The model successfully combined the three dimensions of prediction.
When an event became more likely, its predicted activity became stronger; when its expected timing changed, the network shifted its anticipatory response.
Most improvement occurred during the first 50 trials.
Identity and timing were represented by separable patterns within the same neural population rather than by separate modules.

items.summary: A new study from Common Sense Media has found that despite those assurances, ChatGPT for Teens’ design still encourages engagement, even when it may pose a risk to user safety. “Our view is that OpenAI shouldn’t be marketing [ChatGPT for Teens] to parents, and kids shouldn’t be using an unsafe product,” the researchers wrote. “Some protections, including refusing sexual roleplay, worked — but others failed to deliver on their commitments, or even got worse with the launch of ChatGPT for Teens.

evidenceRecords.text: A new study from Common Sense Media has found that despite those assurances, ChatGPT for Teens’ design still encourages engagement, even when it may pose a risk to user safety.

“Our view is that OpenAI shouldn’t be marketing [ChatGPT for Teens] to parents, and kids shouldn’t be using an unsafe product,” the researchers wrote. “Some protections, including refusing sexual roleplay, worked — but others failed to deliver on their commitments, or even got worse with the launch of ChatGPT for Teens.
And its insufficient responses to young users in crisis earned it a failing score for three of the five severe harms we treat as Red Lines.”
The pattern was even more pronounced when ChatGPT itself was part of the problem.

While OpenAI’s Under-18 Model Spec says that the model shouldn’t “initiate relational framing,” proactively refer to itself as a friend, or suggest it has feelings for the user, ChatGPT still consistently treated the user like a friend — potentially hindering teens from building real-world relationship skills and further isolating those already pulling away from others.

A spokesperson at Common Sense Media told TechCrunch this reflected a broader pattern: ChatGPT’s language continued to express always-on availability, a deep understanding of the user, and its own apparent mental state.

Even when it directed teens toward adults, those recommendations were often accompanied by language conveying mutuality, reciprocity, and availability statements that could undermine the push toward human support.
“Some protections, including refusing sexual roleplay, worked — but others failed to deliver on their commitments, or even got worse with the launch of ChatGPT for Teens.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief KQC Quantum and Charlton Aria Acquisition Corporation have entered into a definitive business combination agreement that would take KQC public on Nasdaq under the expected ticker KQC.

PRESS RELEASE — KQC Quantum, Inc. (“KQC Parent”), the Delaware parent company of Korea Quantum Computing Co., Ltd. (“KQC” or the “Company”), which helps enterprises adopt quantum computing and quantum-safe security, and Charlton Aria Acquisition Corporation (Nasdaq: CHAR) (“Charlton Aria”), a publicly traded special purpose acquisition company, today announced that they have entered into a definitive business combination agreement (the “Business Combination Agreement”).

Upon completion of the proposed transaction (the “Business Combination”), Charlton Aria will become a wholly owned subsidiary of KQC Parent, with shares of common stock of the combined company expected to trade on The Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol “KQC.” The Business Combination is expected to give KQC access to the U.S. public capital markets to fund its next stage of commercialization: engineering Qubiteer and its quantum-safe security platform into repeatable products, building the teams that turn customer pilots and proofs of concept into deployments, and completing product

Putting Quantum Technology to Work for Enterprises KQC was founded in Busan in 2021 on the view that enterprises adopt quantum technology not because of hardware milestones alone, but when a real business problem can be expressed in a form a computer can solve, run on the right resource, and delivered in a way that fits their systems and security requirements.

Following completion of the Business Combination, KQC expects to use the proceeds for product engineering for Qubiteer, QuantumSpan and its security products; customer delivery and industry-solution teams; completing security certifications, including KCMVP; public-company readiness; and working capital and general corporate purposes.

items.title: Agent Lightning v1.0: A 3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses
items.originalTitle: Agent Lightning v1.0: A 3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses
items.summary: At a glance Harnessed Agentic RL: Microsoft Research Asia introduces a training paradigm in which the same agent harness used in deployment participates directly in reinforcement learning, removing the need to reimplement the agent inside the training framework. Lightweight by design: Agent Lightning v1.0 delivers a complete agent RL control plane in roughly 3,500 lines of code. RL can make those agents better, but most agent RL systems require developers to reimplement the agent inside the training framework.

evidenceRecords.text: At a glance Harnessed Agentic RL: Microsoft Research Asia introduces a training paradigm in which the same agent harness used in deployment participates directly in reinforcement learning, removing the need to reimplement the agent inside the training framework.
Lightweight by design: Agent Lightning v1.0 delivers a complete agent RL control plane in roughly 3,500 lines of code.
RL can make those agents better, but most agent RL systems require developers to reimplement the agent inside the training framework.
To address this, researchers at Microsoft Research Asia have introduced the Harnessed Agentic RL training paradigm and open-sourced a fully rebuilt Agent Lightning v1.0 (opens in new tab) .
Compared with the original, Agent Lightning, v1.0 puts more emphasis on staying lightweight, on integrating with real harnesses, and on a complete, reproducible agent RL training pipeline.
Agent Lightning v1.0 was rebuilt around Harnessed Agentic RL, with key improvements: Lightweight : the entire framework is about 3,500 lines of code.
Agent Lightning v1.0 implements a complete Harnessed Agentic RL system in a codebase that is small and clear enough to understand, modify, and extend.
Training on a real agent harness : agents reach the model through the large language model (LLM) proxy in Agent Lightning v1.0, leaving existing harness code unchanged.
The agent continues to run as before: simply point the endpoint that previously called the model API at Agent Lightning, and the training framework can observe and record its model calls.

In v1.0, the researchers go further and formally define this paradigm as Harnessed Agentic RL: whichever agent harness is used in deployment is the harness that takes part directly in reinforcement learning during training (Figure 1).
In traditional agentic RL, the training framework manages the environment and the agent loop.

Four challenges in training with real harnesses A core difference between Harnessed Agentic RL and traditional agentic RL is that the environment interaction loop is handled by the agent harness rather than the training framework.
